When I was young I got terrible migraines all the time. Like debilitating wanted to smash my head. Got CT scans, tests, etc. There are dietary triggers, and my lower jaw was slightly misaligned off center from my upper so they thought that was causing some problems.

My teeth were fairly straight but I got braces, rubber bands, etc to line everything back up. Headaches dissipated. If I talk a bunch or keep my mouth open for an extended period of time (like at the dentist getting a cleaning) then I'm guaranteed a headache, but they're never quite as severe, especially since I know what to avoid/how to alleviate them a bit better now.

Drink water, and take Excedrin. Excedrin (or offbrand) is the best for my headaches. I think it's the caffeine.

I imagine the pain being a liquid filling up my head. I really concentrate on this image and try to associate the pain with this image. Which, for a long time, was difficult to do while I was also praying for a quick death. Then, I'd picture a spigot in my temple opening up, and the pain draining away. Please tell me this is sarcasm. (I really hope it is.)

At first glance, that shit is whack. But there are some different possibilities here, and possibly extenuating circumstances. Were the kids running about and breaking shit, or were they just sitting there? Also, was she really always in the line of sight? Because if she was, and they were sitting there without causing a disturbance, I don't see the problem here. Two years old is much too young to be left alone, but with a 6 year old sibling, eh....debatable. But on the other hand, how can you really do a job interview, which takes all of your attention, and split your attention between the interview and watching the kids, so maybe also within sight, but not at all attentive. Also, how was the cop standing there? Was he asking the children where their parents were or was he camping out just watching and waiting? Was he visibly involved with the children in such a way where the mother should have been curious, but didn't show up? Really it depends on the details, and we need more information to make an informed opinion and unfortunately no one was there to see.
I think it's a stretch to use abandonment laws in this case. Was it excellent parenting? Negatory. But I doubt this is the purpose of the law.
